title: a struct initialized field by field destroys a field that was never set
reproducer:
struct Res(Movable):
    var id: Int

    def __init__(out self, id: Int):
        self.id = id

    def __del__(deinit self):
        print("drop", self.id)


struct Two(Movable):
    var a: Res
    var b: Res

    def __init__(out self):
        self.a = Res(1)
        self.b = Res(2)


def main():
    var t: Two
    t.a = Res(1)
    print(t.a.id)
compiler: prints `1`, `drop 1`, `drop 0`, as 1.2.0 did: it runs the destructor of t.b, which was never initialized
fixed: rejects the program, as the compiler rejects a variable with a field moved out ("field 't.a' destroyed out of the middle of a value, preventing the overall value from being destroyed"): a variable that ends with only some of its fields set is rejected, however it got there (R, ruled by the human on 2026-11-19)
model: rejects it as partiallyDestroyed, as the fixed compiler would. The model does not read the deprecated `__del__`, which it rejects as invalidSelf; with `__del__` spelled `__deinit__`, it rejects the program as partiallyDestroyed

confirmation.notes: R, the fixed behaviour ruled on 2026-11-19, is provisional: the human will confirm it with Modular's engineers, and the model changes if that discussion changes the semantics.
